compareCandidate.label: Kidney filter vs. coffee filter
compareCandidate.description: Like a coffee filter, the kidney separates wanted from unwanted - but it is far smarter: it actively decides what to keep (water, salts, sugar the body needs) and what to discard (waste).

processes: Returning cleaned blood to the body
plainLanguageExplanation: The kidneys are two bean-shaped organs at the back of the abdomen, one on each side of the spine. Their job is to filter the blood. Every few minutes all of your blood passes through the kidneys, where tiny filtering units called nephrons take out waste products and extra water. That waste becomes urine, which travels through tubes to the bladder to be stored and later released. The kidneys also help keep the right balance of water and salts in your body and make hormones that help control blood pressure and make red blood cells. When your kidneys filter, the cleaned blood returns to your circulation.

whyItMatters: The kidneys keep your blood clean and your body balanced. Understanding them explains what urine is, why staying hydrated matters, and how the body gets rid of its waste safely.
didYouKnow: Your kidneys filter about 180 liters of fluid a day - but you only pee out about 1-2 liters, because almost all of it gets reabsorbed.
